answer: Price agent identity by verifiable work, not account count. Before an agent can act as a vertex in payment or voting graphs, it must earn reputation through attested tasks: a newcomer starts hollow, with no history, no delegation, and capped limits. Reaching the zenith of trust, large transfers or governance weight, demands a long, costly trail of successful peer-attested work that cannot be copied across clones. An attacker spinning up thousands of identities faces the same grind per identity, so forging influence scales linearly in cost while honest agents compound trust.
